newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse stronger after crisis - EconMin says.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse stronger after crisis - EconMin says.

text.p: The Athens bourse will come out stronger after the recent Delta Securities settlement scandal, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou said on Monday.

"The Athens Stock Exchange will come out stronger from its recent crisis which will be seen eventually as a crisis of cleansing and modernisation," he told a conference on the Greek economy organised by American-Hellenic Chamber of Commerce.
The recent turmoil stemmed from the implementation of two new laws aimed at better regulating the market and ensuring proper settlement of accounts, he said.
Papandoniou, who has been criticised by many brokers for reacting slowly to the settlement scandal, said investigations were underway and vowed that those responsible would be charged.

"The strict implementation of the law and the inspections underway by international auditors and justice officials will lead to the charging of those responsible and will reinforce the credibility of the Athens Stock Exchange," Papandoniou said.
The scandal rocked the bourse when Delta Securities tried to settle at the clearing house with bad cheques.
The Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA) boycotted trade for three days to try to force the government to clean up the settlement system and to guarantee settlement of accounts.
The bourse was out of operation for most of a fourth day when Athens brokerages had to settle accounts at the clearing house before being permitted to trade again.
Three Delta officials were charged with "large-scale and repeated" fraud and the national economy ministry ordered an audit of 10 brokerages after the scandal broke.
Last week an investigating magistrate ordered all brokerages to check their books for 16 specific clients and provide details of all the clients' business since January 1, 1996.

The magistrate wants to find out who was on the other side of the Delta trades, especially shares of the Magrizos textiles firm which have been tied to the scandal. The magistrate is trying to determine whether organised price manipulation took place.
The government has ordered a separate check by international auditors of all 65 brokerages at the bourse. It is expected to get underway this week.
